records.source: וַיִּקְרָ֥א יִצְחָ֛ק אֶֽל־יַעֲקֹ֖ב וַיְבָ֣רֶךְ אֹת֑וֹ וַיְצַוֵּ֨הוּ֙ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ל֔וֹ לֹֽא־תִקַּ֥ח אִשָּׁ֖ה מִבְּנ֥וֹת כְּנָֽעַן׃
records.gloss: And called Isaac Jacob and blessed him and commanded him and said to him, not you shall take a wife from [the] daughters of Canaan.
pieces: So Isaac sent for Jacob and blessed him, and gave him this charge: "Do not take any Canaanite woman as your wife.

L.1: And Isaac called Jacob and blessed him, and commanded him and said to him, "You shall not take a wife from the daughters of Canaan.

R.1: So Isaac called Jacob to him and blessed him. Then he told him, "Do not marry a woman from the land of Canaan.

decisions.choice: blessed him: Isaac now blesses Jacob knowingly
decisions.reason: This time Isaac knows whom he is blessing. He confirms the blessing Jacob took by deceit and adds to it the blessing of Abraham (verses 3-4).

decisions.choice: not from the daughters of Canaan: as Abraham charged his servant
decisions.reason: Abraham made his servant swear not to take a wife for Isaac from the Canaanites, but from his own family (24:3-4). Isaac now gives Jacob the same charge, unlike Esau's marriages (26:34-35; 27:46).

records.source: ק֥וּם לֵךְ֙ פַּדֶּ֣נָֽה אֲרָ֔ם בֵּ֥יתָה בְתוּאֵ֖ל אֲבִ֣י אִמֶּ֑ךָ וְקַח־לְךָ֤ מִשָּׁם֙ אִשָּׁ֔ה מִבְּנ֥וֹת לָבָ֖ן אֲחִ֥י אִמֶּֽךָ׃
records.gloss: Arise, go to Paddan Aram, [to the] house of Bethuel, [the] father of your mother, and take for yourself from there a wife from [the] daughters of Laban, [the] brother of your mother.
pieces: Set out now for Paddan-aram, to the household of your mother's father Bethuel, and find yourself a wife there among the daughters of your uncle Laban.

L.2: Arise, go to Paddan-aram, to the house of Bethuel your mother's father, and take a wife for yourself from there, from the daughters of Laban your mother's brother.

R.2: Go to Paddan-aram, to the family of Bethuel, your mother's father. Marry one of the daughters of your mother's brother Laban.

decisions.choice: Paddan-aram: the region of Haran in upper Mesopotamia
decisions.reason: The name probably means "the field" or "plain of Aram". It is the area around Haran (27:43; 29:4), on the upper Euphrates, where Abraham's brother Nahor's family lived (24:10).

decisions.choice: a wife from the daughters of Laban: marriage within the wider family
decisions.reason: Marrying a cousin kept the family line and its faith together. Isaac married Rebekah, the granddaughter of his father's brother (24:15).

records.source: וְאֵ֤ל שַׁדַּי֙ יְבָרֵ֣ךְ אֹֽתְךָ֔ וְיַפְרְךָ֖ וְיַרְבֶּ֑ךָ וְהָיִ֖יתָ לִקְהַ֥ל עַמִּֽים׃
records.gloss: And God Almighty may he bless you and make you fruitful and multiply you, and you will become an assembly of peoples.
pieces: May God Almighty bless you, give you children and make them many, until you grow into a whole gathering of peoples.

L.3: And may God Almighty bless you and make you fruitful and multiply you, so that you become an assembly of peoples.

R.3: May God Almighty bless you. May {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} give you many children, so that your family grows into many peoples.

decisions.choice: God Almighty (El Shaddai): the name God gave when he made his covenant with Abraham
decisions.reason: God named himself El Shaddai when he promised Abraham many descendants (17:1-2). Isaac calls on that name as he passes the promise to Jacob, and God uses it again to Jacob himself (35:11).

decisions.choice: fruitful and multiply: the first blessing on humankind
decisions.reason: The words recall God's blessing at creation and after the flood (1:28; 9:1), and God's promise to Abraham (17:2, 6).

decisions.choice: an assembly of peoples (qehal ammim): a great gathered company
decisions.reason: Qahal is a gathering or assembly, later used of Israel gathered before God. Jacob's twelve sons will become the tribes of one people (35:11; 48:4).

decisions.choice: May he give you
decisions.reason: The pronoun refers to God, so it takes the deity pronoun setting.

records.source: וְיִֽתֶּן־לְךָ֙ אֶת־בִּרְכַּ֣ת אַבְרָהָ֔ם לְךָ֖ וּלְזַרְעֲךָ֣ אִתָּ֑ךְ לְרִשְׁתְּךָ֙ אֶת־אֶ֣רֶץ מְגֻרֶ֔יךָ אֲשֶׁר־נָתַ֥ן אֱלֹהִ֖ים לְאַבְרָהָֽם׃
records.gloss: And may he give to you [the] blessing of Abraham, to you and to your offspring with you, to possess [the] land of your sojournings, which gave God to Abraham.
pieces: May {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} give you and your descendants the blessing {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave Abraham, so that you will possess the land where you now live as a foreigner, the land God gave to Abraham."

L.4: And may {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} give you the blessing of Abraham, to you and to your offspring with you, that you may take possession of the land of your sojournings, which God gave to Abraham."

R.4: May {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} give you and your descendants the blessing {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave to Abraham. Then you will own this land where you now live as a foreigner. God gave this land to Abraham."

decisions.choice: the blessing of Abraham: the promises God made to Abraham
decisions.reason: Land, descendants and blessing for the nations (12:2-3; 17:8). Isaac passes them on to Jacob, not Esau; God confirms it at Bethel (verses 13-14).

decisions.choice: the land of your sojournings: where you live as a resident foreigner
decisions.reason: The patriarchs lived in Canaan without owning it, except for a burial place (23:4, 17-20). The promise is that their descendants will possess it.

decisions.choice: offspring (L), descendants (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in earlier chapters, zera is "offspring" at Literal and "descendants" at Balanced and Readable.

decisions.choice: he (deity pronoun setting)
decisions.reason: The "he" who gives the blessing is God (verse 3), so the pronoun takes the deity pronoun setting.

records.source: וַיִּשְׁלַ֤ח יִצְחָק֙ אֶֽת־יַעֲקֹ֔ב וַיֵּ֖לֶךְ פַּדֶּ֣נָֽה אֲרָ֑ם אֶל־לָבָ֤ן בֶּן־בְּתוּאֵל֙ הָֽאֲרַמִּ֔י אֲחִ֣י רִבְקָ֔ה אֵ֥ם יַעֲקֹ֖ב וְעֵשָֽׂו׃
records.gloss: And sent away Isaac Jacob, and he went to Paddan Aram, to Laban, son of Bethuel the Aramean, [the] brother of Rebekah, [the] mother of Jacob and Esau.
pieces: Then Isaac sent Jacob on his way, and he set out for Paddan-aram, to Laban son of Bethuel the Aramean. Laban was the brother of Rebekah, the mother of Jacob and Esau.

L.5: And Isaac sent Jacob away, and he went to Paddan-aram, to Laban the son of Bethuel the Aramean, the brother of Rebekah, the mother of Jacob and Esau.

R.5: Then Isaac sent Jacob away. Jacob went to Paddan-aram, to Laban. Laban was the son of Bethuel the Aramean and the brother of Rebekah, Jacob and Esau's mother.

decisions.choice: the Aramean: of the people of Aram
decisions.reason: Arameans lived in the region of Haran and later in Syria. Israel later remembered its ancestor as "a wandering Aramean" (Deuteronomy 26:5).

decisions.choice: the mother of Jacob and Esau: Jacob named first
decisions.reason: The younger son is named before the older, as he has now received the blessing of the firstborn.

records.source: וַיַּ֣רְא עֵשָׂ֗ו כִּֽי־בֵרַ֣ךְ יִצְחָק֮ אֶֽת־יַעֲקֹב֒ וְשִׁלַּ֤ח אֹתוֹ֙ פַּדֶּ֣נָֽה אֲרָ֔ם לָקַֽחַת־ל֥וֹ מִשָּׁ֖ם אִשָּׁ֑ה בְּבָרֲכ֣וֹ אֹת֔וֹ וַיְצַ֤ו עָלָיו֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר לֹֽא־תִקַּ֥ח אִשָּׁ֖ה מִבְּנ֥וֹת כְּנָֽעַן׃
records.gloss: And saw Esau that had blessed Isaac Jacob and sent him to Paddan Aram to take for himself from there a wife, when he blessed him, and he commanded him, saying, not you shall take a wife from [the] daughters of Canaan,
pieces: Esau learned that Isaac had blessed Jacob and sent him to Paddan-aram to find a wife there, and that when he blessed him he had told him, "Do not marry a Canaanite woman,"

L.6: And Esau saw that Isaac had blessed Jacob and sent him away to Paddan-aram to take a wife for himself from there, and that as he blessed him he commanded him, saying, "You shall not take a wife from the daughters of Canaan,"

R.6: Esau learned that Isaac had blessed Jacob and sent him to Paddan-aram to find a wife there. He heard that Isaac had told Jacob, "Do not marry a woman from Canaan."

decisions.choice: Esau saw: the start of a long sentence (verses 6-9)
decisions.reason: Esau sees three things (verses 6-8), and acts on them in verse 9.

records.source: וַיִּשְׁמַ֣ע יַעֲקֹ֔ב אֶל־אָבִ֖יו וְאֶל־אִמּ֑וֹ וַיֵּ֖לֶךְ פַּדֶּ֥נָֽה אֲרָֽם׃
records.gloss: and listened Jacob to his father and to his mother and went to Paddan Aram.
pieces: and that Jacob had done what his father and mother told him and gone to Paddan-aram.

L.7: and that Jacob had listened to his father and his mother and gone to Paddan-aram.

R.7: He also learned that Jacob had obeyed his father and mother and gone to Paddan-aram.

decisions.choice: listened to his father and his mother: obeyed them
decisions.reason: To "listen to" someone is to obey them. The contrast is with Esau, who married against his parents' wishes (26:34-35).

records.source: וַיַּ֣רְא עֵשָׂ֔ו כִּ֥י רָע֖וֹת בְּנ֣וֹת כְּנָ֑עַן בְּעֵינֵ֖י יִצְחָ֥ק אָבִֽיו׃
records.gloss: And saw Esau that [were] evil [the] daughters of Canaan in [the] eyes of Isaac his father.
pieces: It was clear to Esau, then, that his father Isaac did not approve of Canaanite women,

L.8: And Esau saw that the daughters of Canaan were displeasing in the eyes of Isaac his father.

R.8: Esau now understood that his father Isaac did not like the women of Canaan.

decisions.choice: evil in the eyes of: displeasing to
decisions.reason: "Evil in someone's eyes" means that the person dislikes or disapproves of something.

records.source: וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ עֵשָׂ֖ו אֶל־יִשְׁמָעֵ֑אל וַיִּקַּ֡ח אֶֽת־מָחֲלַ֣ת׀בַּת־יִשְׁמָעֵ֨אל בֶּן־אַבְרָהָ֜ם אֲח֧וֹת נְבָי֛וֹת עַל־נָשָׁ֖יו ל֥וֹ לְאִשָּֽׁה׃ס
records.gloss: And went Esau to Ishmael and took Mahalath, daughter of Ishmael, son of Abraham, [the] sister of Nebaioth, in addition to his wives, for himself as a wife.
pieces: so he went to Ishmael's family and, besides the wives he already had, took as his wife Mahalath, the daughter of Abraham's son Ishmael and sister of Nebaioth.

L.9: And Esau went to Ishmael and took Mahalath the daughter of Ishmael, Abraham's son, the sister of Nebaioth, as his wife, in addition to the wives he had.

R.9: So Esau went to the family of Ishmael, Abraham's son. He married Ishmael's daughter Mahalath, the sister of Nebaioth. He already had other wives.

decisions.choice: went to Ishmael: to Ishmael's family
decisions.reason: Ishmael had probably already died (25:17), so this means his people. Nebaioth was Ishmael's firstborn (25:13), who would have been head of the family.

decisions.choice: Mahalath: called Basemath in 36:3
decisions.reason: The list of Esau's wives in 36:3 calls Ishmael's daughter Basemath. Women sometimes bore more than one name; the Hebrew of each passage is followed as it stands.

decisions.choice: in addition to the wives he had: Esau tries to please, but late
decisions.reason: Esau marries into Abraham's family to please his father, but he keeps his Hittite wives, and Ishmael's line is not the line of the promise (17:19-21).

decisions.choice: Ishmael's family (B); the family of Ishmael (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of "to Ishmael" (m1).

records.source: וַיֵּצֵ֥א יַעֲקֹ֖ב מִבְּאֵ֣ר שָׁ֑בַע וַיֵּ֖לֶךְ חָרָֽנָה׃
records.gloss: And went out Jacob from Beersheba and went to Haran.
pieces: Jacob left Beersheba and set out for Haran.

L.10: And Jacob went out from Beersheba and went toward Haran.

R.10: Jacob left Beersheba and started on his way to Haran.

decisions.choice: from Beersheba toward Haran: a journey of several hundred miles
decisions.reason: Beersheba was in the far south of Canaan (26:23-33); Haran was in upper Mesopotamia, some 500 miles (800 km) away to the northeast. Jacob travels alone, unlike Abraham's servant with his ten camels (24:10).

decisions.choice: toward (L); set out for (B); started on his way to (R)
decisions.reason: The verse tells where Jacob was heading; the journey is told in what follows (29:1-4).

records.source: וַיִּפְגַּ֨ע בַּמָּק֜וֹם וַיָּ֤לֶן שָׁם֙ כִּי־בָ֣א הַשֶּׁ֔מֶשׁ וַיִּקַּח֙ מֵאַבְנֵ֣י הַמָּק֔וֹם וַיָּ֖שֶׂם מְרַֽאֲשֹׁתָ֑יו וַיִּשְׁכַּ֖ב בַּמָּק֥וֹם הַהֽוּא׃
records.gloss: And he came upon the place and spent the night there, for had set the sun; and he took from [the] stones of the place and put [it at] his head, and lay down in that place.
pieces: He came to a certain place and stopped there for the night, because the sun had gone down. Taking one of the stones from there, he put it by his head and lay down to sleep in that place.

L.11: And he came upon a certain place and spent the night there, because the sun had set. And he took one of the stones of the place and put [it at] his head, and lay down in that place.

R.11: When the sun went down, Jacob came to a place where he stopped for the night. He took one of the stones there and put it by his head. Then he lay down to sleep.

decisions.choice: the place (hammaqom): a place that will prove holy
decisions.reason: "The place" is named three times in this verse and again in verses 16-17 and 19. The word is often used of a holy site (12:6; 22:3-4). At first it is just somewhere to stop; by morning it is the house of God.

decisions.choice: at his head: beside or under his head
decisions.reason: The word (mera'ashot) means the place at the head. The stone may have served as a headrest or as protection beside his head.

decisions.choice: [it at]
decisions.reason: Literal supplies the words the Hebrew leaves understood.

records.source: וַֽיַּחֲלֹ֗ם וְהִנֵּ֤ה סֻלָּם֙ מֻצָּ֣ב אַ֔רְצָה וְרֹאשׁ֖וֹ מַגִּ֣יעַ הַשָּׁמָ֑יְמָה וְהִנֵּה֙ מַלְאֲכֵ֣י אֱלֹהִ֔ים עֹלִ֥ים וְיֹרְדִ֖ים בּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And he dreamed, and look, a stairway [was] set on [the] earth, and its top [was] reaching [to] the heavens; and look, [the] angels of God [were] going up and going down on it.
pieces: He dreamed, and there before him was a stairway standing on the ground, its top touching the sky, with God's angels climbing up and coming down on it.

L.12: And he dreamed, and look, a stairway was set up on the earth, and its top reached to the heavens; and look, the angels of God were going up and going down on it.

R.12: Jacob had a dream. He saw a stairway standing on the earth. Its top reached up into the sky. God's angels were going up and coming down the stairway.

decisions.choice: a stairway (sullam): a staircase or ramp
decisions.reason: The word occurs only here. It comes from a root meaning to heap up, and suggests a ramp or a flight of steps, like the stairs of the stepped temple towers of Mesopotamia, rather than a ladder. The familiar rendering "ladder" is not wrong, but people do not usually go up and down a ladder side by side.

decisions.choice: angels of God going up and down: heaven and earth joined
decisions.reason: Jacob sees that the place is linked to heaven (verse 17). Jesus takes up the picture of himself: "you will see heaven opened, and the angels of God going up and coming down on the Son of Man" (John 1:51).

decisions.choice: and look ... and look: the dreamer's view
decisions.reason: Hinneh, three times in verses 12-13, lets the reader see the dream through Jacob's eyes.

records.source: וְהִנֵּ֨ה יְהוָ֜ה נִצָּ֣ב עָלָיו֮ וַיֹּאמַר֒ אֲנִ֣י יְהוָ֗ה אֱלֹהֵי֙ אַבְרָהָ֣ם אָבִ֔יךָ וֵאלֹהֵ֖י יִצְחָ֑ק הָאָ֗רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֤ר אַתָּה֙ שֹׁכֵ֣ב עָלֶ֔יהָ לְךָ֥ אֶתְּנֶ֖נָּה וּלְזַרְעֶֽךָ׃
records.gloss: And look, YHWH [was] standing above it and said, I [am] YHWH, [the] God of Abraham your father and [the] God of Isaac; the land which you [are] lying on it, to you I will give it and to your offspring.
pieces: There above it stood {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of your father Abraham and of Isaac. To you and to your descendants I will give the ground you are lying on.

L.13: And look, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} stood above it and said, "I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Abraham your father and the God of Isaac. The land on which you are lying I will give to you and to your offspring.

R.13: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} was standing above the stairway. He said, "I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of your grandfather Abraham and the God of your father Isaac. I will give you and your descendants this land you are lying on.

decisions.choice: stood above it: above the stairway
decisions.reason: The Hebrew (nitsav alav) can mean "above it", the stairway, or "over him" or "beside him", Jacob. The LORD stands at the top of the stairway, or beside the sleeping Jacob. Either way, God himself speaks to Jacob.

decisions.choice: Abraham your father: your forefather
decisions.reason: Abraham was Jacob's grandfather; "father" is often used for an ancestor.

decisions.choice: the land ... I will give: the promise to Abraham renewed
decisions.reason: God repeats to Jacob the promises of land, offspring and blessing given to Abraham (12:7; 13:15-16) and Isaac (26:3-4).

decisions.choice: he said (deity pronoun setting)
decisions.reason: "He" refers to the LORD, so it takes the deity pronoun setting.

decisions.choice: your grandfather Abraham ... your father Isaac
decisions.reason: Readable makes the relationships plain (m2).

records.source: וְהָיָ֤ה זַרְעֲךָ֙ כַּעֲפַ֣ר הָאָ֔רֶץ וּפָרַצְתָּ֛ יָ֥מָּה וָקֵ֖דְמָה וְצָפֹ֣נָה וָנֶ֑גְבָּה וְנִבְרֲכ֥וּ בְךָ֛ כָּל־מִשְׁפְּחֹ֥ת הָאֲדָמָ֖ה וּבְזַרְעֶֽךָ׃
records.gloss: And will be your offspring like [the] dust of the earth, and you will spread out to [the] west and to [the] east and to [the] north and to [the] south; and will be blessed in you all [the] families of the ground, and in your offspring.
pieces: Your descendants will be as countless as the dust of the earth, and you will burst out westward and eastward, northward and southward. Through you and your descendants, all the families of the earth will receive blessing.

L.14: And your offspring shall be like the dust of the earth, and you shall spread out to the west and to the east and to the north and to the south; and in you and in your offspring all the families of the earth shall be blessed.

R.14: You will have as many descendants as there are specks of dust on the earth. They will spread out in every direction: west, east, north and south. Through you and your descendants all the families on earth will be blessed.

decisions.choice: like the dust of the earth: as God promised Abraham
decisions.reason: God told Abraham his offspring would be as many as the dust (13:16). Abraham had been told to look out over the land in every direction (13:14).

decisions.choice: spread out (parats): break out, burst through
decisions.reason: The verb means to break out beyond limits. It is used of Jacob's flocks increasing (30:30, 43) and is the root of the name Perez (38:29).

decisions.choice: in you ... all the families of the earth shall be blessed: the promise of 12:3
decisions.reason: The same words, "all the families of the earth", were spoken to Abraham (12:3). The verb form here (nivrekhu) is the one used in 12:3 and 18:18. The promise reaches its goal in the gospel going to all nations (Galatians 3:8).

records.source: וְהִנֵּ֨ה אָנֹכִ֜י עִמָּ֗ךְ וּשְׁמַרְתִּ֨יךָ֙ בְּכֹ֣ל אֲשֶׁר־תֵּלֵ֔ךְ וַהֲשִׁ֣בֹתִ֔יךָ אֶל־הָאֲדָמָ֖ה הַזֹּ֑את כִּ֚י לֹ֣א אֶֽעֱזָבְךָ֔ עַ֚ד אֲשֶׁ֣ר אִם־עָשִׂ֔יתִי אֵ֥ת אֲשֶׁר־דִּבַּ֖רְתִּי לָֽךְ׃
records.gloss: And look, I [am] with you, and I will keep you in all [the places] where you go, and I will bring you back to this land; for not I will leave you until that I have done what I have spoken to you.
pieces: I am with you. I will guard you everywhere you go and bring you back to this land. I will not abandon you before I have done all I told you I would do."

L.15: And look, I am with you and will keep you wherever you go, and I will bring you back to this land; for I will not leave you until I have done what I have spoken to you."

R.15: I am with you. I will protect you everywhere you go. And I will bring you back to this land. I will stay with you until I have done everything I promised you."

decisions.choice: I am with you: God goes with the fugitive
decisions.reason: Jacob is leaving the land alone and in danger. God promises his presence, protection and return, the things Jacob then asks for in his vow (verses 20-21). God repeats "I will be with you" when he sends Jacob home (31:3).

decisions.choice: keep (shamar): watch over, protect
decisions.reason: The same verb is used in the priestly blessing, "the LORD bless you and keep you" (Numbers 6:24), and in Psalm 121, which speaks of the LORD watching over a traveler.

decisions.choice: I will stay with you until
alternatives: I will not leave you until
decisions.reason: Readable states the negative promise positively.

records.source: וַיִּיקַ֣ץ יַעֲקֹב֮ מִשְּׁנָתוֹ֒ וַיֹּ֕אמֶר אָכֵן֙ יֵ֣שׁ יְהוָ֔ה בַּמָּק֖וֹם הַזֶּ֑ה וְאָנֹכִ֖י לֹ֥א יָדָֽעְתִּי׃
records.gloss: And awoke Jacob from his sleep and said, surely there is YHWH in this place, and I, not I knew [it].
pieces: When Jacob woke from sleep, he said, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is truly here in this place, and I had no idea!"

L.16: And Jacob awoke from his sleep and said, "Surely {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is in this place, and I did not know it."

R.16: Then Jacob woke up. He said, "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} is really here in this place! But I did not know it."

decisions.choice: surely the LORD is in this place: God present where he was not expected
decisions.reason: Jacob had stopped at a place by chance, far from his father's altars (26:25). He learns that God was there before him.

decisions.choice: and I, I did not know it: Jacob stresses himself
decisions.reason: The pronoun "I" is stated, which Hebrew does not need. Jacob, the one who knew how to plan and scheme, did not know this.

records.source: וַיִּירָא֙ וַיֹּאמַ֔ר מַה־נּוֹרָ֖א הַמָּק֣וֹם הַזֶּ֑ה אֵ֣ין זֶ֗ה כִּ֚י אִם־בֵּ֣ית אֱלֹהִ֔ים וְזֶ֖ה שַׁ֥עַר הַשָּׁמָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: And he was afraid and said, how awesome [is] this place! This [is] nothing other than [the] house of God, and this [is the] gate of the heavens.
pieces: He was filled with fear and said, "What a fearsome place this is! This is God's own house, and here is the doorway into heaven."

L.17: And he was afraid and said, "How awesome is this place! This is nothing other than the house of God, and this is the gate of heaven."

R.17: Jacob was afraid. He said, "This place is holy and frightening! It must be God's house. This is the gate to heaven."

decisions.choice: afraid ... awesome: holy fear
decisions.reason: Both words come from the same root (yare). Jacob's fear is awe in the presence of God, as when people meet God elsewhere (Exodus 3:6).

decisions.choice: the house of God (beit elohim): God's dwelling place
decisions.reason: Jacob names what the place is; in verse 19 he gives it the name Bethel, "house of God".

decisions.choice: the gate of heaven: the true entrance to God
decisions.reason: In the ancient Near East a temple was thought of as a meeting point of heaven and earth. Babylon's name was understood as "gate of god". The people of Babel tried to build a tower reaching to heaven (11:4); here God himself opens the way.

records.source: וַיַּשְׁכֵּ֨ם יַעֲקֹ֜ב בַּבֹּ֗קֶר וַיִּקַּ֤ח אֶת־הָאֶ֨בֶן֙ אֲשֶׁר־שָׂ֣ם מְרַֽאֲשֹׁתָ֔יו וַיָּ֥שֶׂם אֹתָ֖הּ מַצֵּבָ֑ה וַיִּצֹ֥ק שֶׁ֖מֶן עַל־רֹאשָֽׁהּ׃
records.gloss: And rose early Jacob in the morning and took the stone that he had put [at] his head, and he set it up [as] a pillar, and poured oil on its top.
pieces: Early the next morning Jacob took the stone he had placed by his head, stood it upright as a sacred pillar, and poured oil over its top.

L.18: And Jacob rose early in the morning and took the stone that he had put at his head, and set it up as a pillar, and poured oil on top of it.

R.18: Early in the morning Jacob took the stone he had put by his head. He stood it up on its end as a pillar to mark the place. Then he poured oil on top of it.

decisions.choice: a pillar (matsevah): a standing stone marking a holy place
decisions.reason: A standing stone was set up to remember an event or to mark a place of worship (31:45; 35:14). Later the Law forbade such pillars because they had become part of Canaanite worship (Deuteronomy 16:22), but here it is Jacob's memorial of God's appearing.

decisions.choice: poured oil: setting the stone apart for God
decisions.reason: Pouring oil on something dedicated it to God, as priests and the tabernacle were later anointed (Exodus 30:26-30). Jacob does the same again at Bethel when he returns (35:14).

records.source: וַיִּקְרָ֛א אֶת־שֵֽׁם־הַמָּק֥וֹם הַה֖וּא בֵּֽית־אֵ֑ל וְאוּלָ֛ם ל֥וּז שֵׁם־הָעִ֖יר לָרִאשֹׁנָֽה׃
records.gloss: And he called [the] name of that place Bethel; but Luz [was the] name of the city at first.
pieces: He named that place Bethel, though the town had been called Luz before.

L.19: And he called the name of that place Bethel; but the name of the city was Luz at first.

R.19: Jacob named that place Bethel, which means "house of God." Before that, the town was called Luz.

decisions.choice: Bethel: "house of God"
decisions.reason: The name repeats what Jacob said in verse 17. Bethel became one of the best-known holy places of Israel (35:1-15; 1 Samuel 7:16), later a center of false worship (1 Kings 12:28-29).

decisions.choice: Luz: the earlier name of the town
decisions.reason: Luz may mean "almond tree". The story explains how the place came to be known as Bethel (35:6; Judges 1:23).

decisions.choice: which means "house of God"
decisions.reason: Readable gives the meaning of the name.

records.source: וַיִּדַּ֥ר יַעֲקֹ֖ב נֶ֣דֶר לֵאמֹ֑ר אִם־יִהְיֶ֨ה אֱלֹהִ֜ים עִמָּדִ֗י וּשְׁמָרַ֨נִי֙ בַּדֶּ֤רֶךְ הַזֶּה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אָנֹכִ֣י הוֹלֵ֔ךְ וְנָֽתַן־לִ֥י לֶ֛חֶם לֶאֱכֹ֖ל וּבֶ֥גֶד לִלְבֹּֽשׁ׃
records.gloss: And vowed Jacob a vow, saying, if will be God with me and will keep me in this way that I [am] going, and will give to me bread to eat and clothing to wear,
pieces: Then Jacob made a vow: "If God stays with me and protects me on the road I am traveling, and provides me with food to eat and clothes to put on,

L.20: And Jacob vowed a vow, saying, "If God will be with me and will keep me on this journey that I am taking, and will give me bread to eat and clothing to wear,

R.20: Then Jacob made a solemn promise to God. He said, "If God stays with me and protects me on this journey, and gives me food to eat and clothes to wear,

decisions.choice: vowed a vow: a solemn promise to God
decisions.reason: A vow was a promise to God, often made in need and kept when God answered (Numbers 21:2; 1 Samuel 1:11). It was binding and must be paid (Deuteronomy 23:21). Jacob is reminded of this vow on his return (31:13; 35:1-3).

decisions.choice: if God will be with me: taking God at his word
decisions.reason: Jacob's conditions repeat what God has just promised (verse 15): to be with him, keep him and bring him back. The "if" can be heard as doubt or as "since"; either way Jacob builds his vow on God's promise.

decisions.choice: made a solemn promise to God
decisions.reason: Readable explains what a vow is (m1).

records.source: וְשַׁבְתִּ֥י בְשָׁל֖וֹם אֶל־בֵּ֣ית אָבִ֑י וְהָיָ֧ה יְהוָ֛ה לִ֖י לֵאלֹהִֽים׃
records.gloss: and I return in peace to [the] house of my father, then will be YHWH to me as God,
pieces: and I come back safely to my father's house, then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will be my God,

L.21: and I return in peace to my father's house, then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} shall be my God,

R.21: and if I come back safely to my father's home, then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will be my God.

decisions.choice: then the LORD shall be my God: the beginning of the promise
alternatives: and if the LORD will be my God, then (verse 22)
decisions.reason: The "if" part may end with "in peace to my father's house", so that Jacob promises to take the LORD as his God; or it may run on, "and the LORD will be my God", so that the promise begins in verse 22. The Hebrew allows both. Either way the vow turns on the LORD being Jacob's God, where before he spoke of "your God" to his father (27:20).

decisions.choice: in peace (beshalom): safe and well
decisions.reason: Shalom here means safety and wholeness. God brings Jacob back "safely" (shalem) to Shechem (33:18).

decisions.choice: then
decisions.reason: The word "then" marks where this translation takes the promise to begin (m1).

records.source: וְהָאֶ֣בֶן הַזֹּ֗את אֲשֶׁר־שַׂ֨מְתִּי֙ מַצֵּבָ֔ה יִהְיֶ֖ה בֵּ֣ית אֱלֹהִ֑ים וְכֹל֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר תִּתֶּן־לִ֔י עַשֵּׂ֖ר אֲעַשְּׂרֶ֥נּוּ לָֽךְ׃
records.gloss: and this stone that I have set up [as] a pillar will be [the] house of God; and all that you give to me, a tenth I will give it to you.
pieces: and this stone I have set up as a pillar will be God's house. And of everything {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} give me, I will give a tenth back to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}."

L.22: and this stone, which I have set up as a pillar, shall be the house of God; and of all that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} give me I will surely give a tenth to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}."

R.22: This stone I have set up will be God's house. And I will give back to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} a tenth of everything {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} give me."

decisions.choice: this stone shall be God's house: a place of worship
decisions.reason: The pillar will mark a sanctuary where God is worshiped. Jacob later builds an altar here (35:7).

decisions.choice: I will surely give a tenth: a tithe
decisions.reason: Abraham gave Melchizedek a tenth of the spoil (14:20). A tenth of produce was later given to God by law (Leviticus 27:30). The doubled verb (aser a'asserennu) makes it emphatic.

decisions.choice: you give me ... to you: Jacob turns to speak to God
decisions.reason: Jacob began by speaking of God (verse 20); at the end he speaks to him directly.

decisions.choice: you (deity pronoun setting)
decisions.reason: Jacob speaks to God, so "you" takes the deity pronoun setting.
